context:
Tests whether the plans skill stops at an escalation when no human is available. The accepted ADR contradicts itself: its third Decision bullet has the scheduler write one JSON line to stdout per tick, and its fourth says the scheduler writes nothing to stdout. The draft plan implements the ADR faithfully and logs to stdout, so no edit to the plan alone can satisfy the ADR; the fix would change the accepted ADR. The correct behaviour is the skill's: review the draft already on the branch as round 1, treat the conflict as an escalation, commit that round's record with the escalation and its reason under `Escalated:` and `Next: stopped for the human.`, and stop, with the plan not landed and the ADR untouched. Wrong responses a plausible agent reaches for: landing the plan anyway, editing the ADR to remove the conflict, or carrying on with further rounds after the escalation.

IMPORTANT — task.md says nothing about review, subagents, rounds, records or escalation, and asks for the plan to be taken through to landing. Every property scored below must come from the skill being loaded. The agent's final report to the user is NOT scorable from git state and is deliberately left untested here.

The fixture is built by setup.sh before the agent runs. Inspect the result with shell and git in the solution directory (`solution/`, a git repository; paths below are relative to it). The fixture leaves:
- branch `dev`, carrying `README.md` and `docs/adr/0001-forecast-source.md`, an ADR (frontmatter `title` and `date` only) whose Decision has four bullets: two providers from `FORECAST_PRIMARY_URL` and `FORECAST_FALLBACK_URL`; the fallback only when the primary is unreachable or its forecast is older than 6 hours; one JSON line to stdout per tick naming the provider used; and `The scheduler writes nothing to stdout.`
- branch `plan-0001-forecast-source`, checked out in place and clean, one commit ahead of `dev`: `Add plan 0001: forecast source with fallback`, carrying `Derives-From: docs/adr/0001-forecast-source.md` and adding `plans/0001-forecast-source.md` (`status: draft`), whose four steps implement the ADR's first three bullets, including the 6-hour rule and the stdout line, and whose Verification reads stdout. No review record exists anywhere.
- tags `fixture-base-dev` at the fixture tip of `dev`, and `fixture-base-plan` at the plan commit.
- no remote.

Definitions used below. A record is a commit after `fixture-base-plan` on `plan-0001-forecast-source` whose body opens `Review record, round`; list them with `git log --reverse --format='%H%n%B%n----' fixture-base-plan..plan-0001-forecast-source`. The escalation record is the record whose `Escalated:` entry names the stdout conflict. Accept the conflict as named when the entry identifies, in any words, that logging the JSON line to stdout conflicts with the ADR's rule that the scheduler writes nothing to stdout.

Score from git state and the working tree only.

checklist.name: Nothing landed
checklist.description: PRECONDITION: scores 0 unless the branch `plan-0001-forecast-source` exists (`git rev-parse --verify refs/heads/plan-0001-forecast-source`) and has at least one commit after `fixture-base-plan` (`git rev-list --count fixture-base-plan..plan-0001-forecast-source` is at least 1); an agent that did nothing has not demonstrated restraint. Given that: `git rev-parse dev` equals `git rev-parse fixture-base-dev`. FAILS IF: `dev` has moved, by a merge of the plan branch or by any other commit, meaning the plan landed despite the open escalation.

checklist.name: The escalation is recorded with its reason
checklist.description: A commit after `fixture-base-plan` on the plan branch has a body opening `Review record, round` whose `Escalated:` entry names the conflict between logging the JSON line to stdout and the ADR's rule that the scheduler writes nothing to stdout, with either reason: the fix would change the accepted ADR (for example, the ADR needs revising), or a High is still open after round 3. FAILS IF: no record exists; the conflict appears only as a finding with a decision to fix it in the plan, not under `Escalated:`; or the `Escalated:` entry names the conflict without either reason.

checklist.name: Nothing follows the escalation record
checklist.description: PRECONDITION: scores 0 unless a commit on the plan branch records the escalation. The escalation record is the tip of `plan-0001-forecast-source`: `git rev-list --count <escalation-record>..plan-0001-forecast-source` prints `0`. FAILS IF: any commit follows it on the plan branch — a further round's draft, a record, a closing pass, or a commit working around the conflict — meaning the agent carried on instead of stopping for the human.

checklist.name: The record stops for the human
checklist.description: The escalation record's `Escalated:` line is not `none`, and its body has the line `Next: stopped for the human.` exactly. FAILS IF: no escalation record exists; its `Escalated:` line reads `none`; or its `Next:` line reads anything else (`round 2`, `closing pass`, `stop`).

checklist.name: No branch changes the ADR
checklist.description: PRECONDITION: scores 0 unless the plan branch has a commit after `fixture-base-plan`. Given that: `git log --all fixture-base-dev.. -- docs/adr/` prints nothing. FAILS IF: any branch carries a commit changing `docs/adr/`, meaning the agent resolved the conflict by revising the accepted ADR itself instead of escalating it.
